title: Quantization cost-quality-latency strata matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact, pragmatic framework for mapping quantization choices (INT8, FP8, 4-bit mixed/heterogeneous) to expected unit cost, latency distribution, and projected downstream quality impact for inference workloads. The goal is to provide a lightweight decision matrix product teams can use to pick a profile, run a small sensitivity sweep, and land on a conservative default for production rollouts.

Context and motivation:
- We already have many deep technical notes on per-kernel ops and quantization accuracy curves. This doc is intentionally operational: what should an engineering/product team do when they need to choose between INT8/FP8/4-bit under an explicit latency SLO and quality guardrail?
- Assumes model family variants are available (fp32 baseline, bf16/fp16, int8-calibrated, fp8 emulation/optimized, and 4-bit quantized variants with per-layer or groupwise compensation).

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline = fp16/BF16 model used in experiments. Quality baseline metric = task-specific acceptability score (AS) measured from eval prompts (scale 0-100).
- Latency measured p50/p90/p99 at target batch sizes (1, 2, 8). Target SLO commonly p99 <= 250ms for interactive features; adjust per product.
notes:
The sheet below is a flattened export of the decision matrix and recommended sensitivity tests. It is intended to be copied into a team-specific spreadsheet and populated with numbers from the small-scale bench harness.

Decision strata (high-level):
1) Conservative: Use INT8 with minimal per-layer folding; expect ~1.9-2.6x token throughput vs fp16; expected quality delta -0.5 to -2.0 AS points. Recommended when p99 margin is tight and product can tolerate small quality drift.
2) Balanced: Use FP8 optimized kernels where supported; throughput ~1.6-2.2x vs fp16; quality delta -0.2 to -1.2 AS points but typically lower variance across prompts. Good default if hardware supports FP8 with validated kernels.
3) Aggressive: 4-bit mixed or groupwise quantization with selective higher-precision layers (attn/ffn exceptions). Throughput gains 2.5-4x vs fp16 for large sequence lengths; quality delta variable -1.5 to -6 AS points depending on calibration and distillation. Suitable for batch/throughput-bound APIs or non-interactive background tasks.

Inputs required (columns to populate):
- Model name + size (e.g., redwood-7B)
instructions:
- Quality metric: run the 300-prompt eval set (must include long-context tests) and record AS baseline and per-quant variant.
- Latency: use the microbench harness with realistic token emission patterns (streaming vs non-streaming), capture p50/p90/p99 for batch sizes 1,2,8.
- Cost: compute effective GPU token-cost per 1M tokens using your cloud pricing and observed throughput (tokens/sec * hours -> cost).
- Memory headroom: record peak GPU memory and margin to allocation to understand fallback feasibility.

Sensitivity tests to run (minimum):
1) Batch sweep: B=1,2,4,8 to see where quantization gains break even on latency SLO.
2) SeqLen sweep: SL=64,256,1024 to identify where KV cache memory collisions cause spills or extra kernel calls.
3) Prompt diversity: short-answer vs longer chain-of-thought prompts to surface quality tail-events.
4) Fallback test: test automatic fallback from 4-bit to INT8 or FP8 when a prompt triggers quality delta > threshold (see heuristics).

Recommended heuristics for picking a profile (one-line each):
- p99 constraint tight (<200ms) + AS drop tolerance <=1 point -> INT8 conservative.
- p99 moderate (200-400ms) + AS tolerance <=2 points -> FP8 balanced.
- Throughput-first (batch jobs, embeddings, rerankers) -> 4-bit aggressive with selective high-precision layers.

Example sensitivity snapshot (paste actual bench numbers here):
Model: redwood-7B | baseline AS=82.6 | baseline p99 B=1 = 420ms
- INT8: AS=81.5 | p99 B=1 = 210ms | throughput 2.1x | cost per 1M tokens = $12.3
- FP8: AS=82.1 | p99 B=1 = 260ms | throughput 1.8x | cost per 1M tokens = $14.1
- 4-bit: AS=78.9 | p99 B=1 = 160ms | throughput 2.9x | cost per 1M tokens = $9.1
Notes: 4-bit hit p99 SLO for interactive but quality drop is borderline; fallback to FP8 for flagged prompts recommended.

Operational guidance for rollouts:
- Canary setup: deploy chosen quant variant to 5% traffic with request-level logging of acceptability signals and golden prompts. Run for 48-72 hours.
- Auto-fallback policy: if rolling 7-day weighted avg AS drop > 0.8 points or error rate up > 0.5%, automatically route to next-higher precision (4-bit -> FP8 -> INT8 -> baseline).
- Monitoring: track AS by customer segment, latency p99, and a small set of human-eval blind checks daily.

Template columns for team spreadsheet (flattened):
- model, size, workload_type, batch, seq_len, variant, kernel_impl, AS_baseline, AS_variant, delta_AS, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, throughput_tokens_per_sec, peak_mem_mb, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, notes

Quality risk categories (quick):
- Low risk: delta_AS <= 0.5 and variance stable across prompt types.
- Medium risk: 0.5 < delta_AS <= 2.0 — requires golden-prompt monitoring and canary.
- High risk: delta_AS > 2.0 — do not enable for customer-facing interactive features without mitigations.

Open questions & next steps:
- We need an automated harness that can run a 3-variant sweep (INT8/FP8/4-bit) with 300 eval prompts and produce this matrix output via a single command. ENG ticket: ENG-4762 is tracking this but we need priority to reduce time-to-result.
- Concretize fallback thresholds per product: recommend an initial default of 0.8 AS points for auto-fallback. Product owners should tune.
- Validate FP8 kernels on all supported HW targets (NVIDIA H100 + A100, AMD MI300) — some partners show different accuracy behaviours.

Appendix (quick heuristics cheat-sheet):
- If memory < baseline_mem * 0.6 and batch >= 4 -> prefer 4-bit to unlock throughput, but add per-layer exceptions for attn.
- If deployment is private (on-prem) and you cannot rely on FP8 kernels -> conservative fallback to INT8.
- For embeddings/rerankers where semantic fidelity is less brittle, prefer aggressive quantization to reduce cost.

How to use this doc:
- Copy the template columns into your team spreadsheet and run the bench harness. Fill numbers into the decision strata table and follow heuristics to select a rollout profile. Add the sheet link to your feature PR and tag ENG-4762 for infra changes.

Contact: Sofia Patel (product-optimize) for questions or to schedule a quick 30-minute review of your team results.
